newsitem.title: USA: World Bank's Wolfensohn calls on U.S. to help IDA.
newsitem.headline: World Bank's Wolfensohn calls on U.S. to help IDA.

text.p: World Bank President James Wolfensohn Monday called upon the United States to meet its commitments to the International Development Association.

"Right now, America's level of overseas development assistance has diminished to the point where the U.S. is in the unique position of being the last of the OECD countries in terms of per capita contribution to IDA," Wolfensohn said.

In prepared remarks before an international development conference, Wolfensohn said it was in the United States' economic interest to help fund IDA, the World Bank affiliate that assists the very poorest countries.
He said that developing countries are the fastest growing U.S. export market, already representing 40 percent of U.S. exports that help create job in the United States.
"IDA isn't charity," Wolfensohn said. "It's self interest."
